strengths: Well-motivated problem: The decode-encode loop inefficiency is clearly identified and articulated with information-theoretic reasoning.
Practical contributions with measurable efficiency gains: Bypassing decoders yields 87.7% faster 3D generation and 20.6% faster audio generation, with improved downstream accuracy.
Solid experimental methodology: Multiple datasets, independent runs with error bars, clear modality ablations, and systematic comparison of latent vs. raw synthetic data.
Strong empirical results on tested benchmarks: Latent teacher outperforms raw teacher by 7.39% on Caltech101; MESSy outperforms LUGPI by 3.40%-2.84% across datasets.
Creative validation approach: Normalized Mutual Information analysis provides evidence of emergent alignment with unseen modalities; qualitative analysis shows selective modality usage per class.
Clear presentation: Well-organized narrative with effective pipeline visualization and logical flow.
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: Experiments restricted to small datasets (Imagenette2-320, Caltech101, ImageNet-100); no full ImageNet or modern large-scale benchmarks. Generalizability to realistic scales unclear.
Synthetic-only validation: All auxiliary modalities (3D, audio) are generated; no evaluation on real multimodal datasets. Quality and relevance of synthetic latents to real data unexamined.

Missing critical ablations: K=3 layers for MESSy ablated only in supplementary; no ablations on Perceiver token budget (100), modality dropout rate (p=0.8), or auxiliary head architecture. These are key design choices.

Incomplete theoretical justification: Data Processing Inequality argument introduced informally without rigorous formalization. 'Capacity interference' mentioned but never formally defined or proven to be solved by MESSy.
MESSy design choices lack justification: Why MSE loss for predictive heads? Why is average-pooling the right aggregation? Why are lightweight heads sufficient? These decisions appear ad-hoc.

Synesthesia analysis limitations: NMI metric and cluster scaling (50/150 clusters) choices not justified; unexplained discrepancy between Deep and HC features; qualitative validation based on only 3 anecdotal examples per category.
Limited technical novelty: Individual components (Perceiver, predictive distillation, latent extraction) are established; MESSy is an incremental variant of existing feature-level distillation.

Experimental design concerns: Raw data baseline using PointNet++ and Mel-spectrograms may unfairly handicap the comparison. No comparison with recent feature distillation methods (RKD, FT, VID). Only 3 runs may lack statistical power for some comparisons.
Dependency on external generative models: No sensitivity analysis across different 3D/audio generators or versions. Reproducibility of synthetic pipeline questionable.

Generalization questions unanswered: Works only on image classification with 3D+audio; unclear for other modalities (depth, infrared), datasets with weak 3D/audio correlations, or larger models and datasets.

strengths: Clear problem identification: The Decode-Encode Loop inefficiency is well-motivated; the Data Processing Inequality framing provides intuitive justification.
Well-structured methodology with clear presentation: Figures 1-2 effectively communicate the three-phase approach (latent generation → multimodal teacher training → MESSy distillation).
Comprehensive ablations within scope: Table 2 demonstrates orthogonal modality contributions, and Section 4.2 provides NMI-based evidence of emergent structural alignment with unobserved modalities.
Multimodal breadth: Extension to 3D and audio latents (beyond text-image) demonstrates ambition compared to existing LUGPI work.
Rigorous experimental design: Three independent runs per experiment with standard deviations; multiple datasets with consistent trend.

Qualitative insights on selective prior usage: Figure 4 shows models preferentially use acoustic priors for sound-distinctive classes and geometric priors for morphologically complex species, suggesting genuine cross-modal association learning.
Computational efficiency gains are real: Documented savings of 87.7% for 3D generation and 20.6% for audio generation translate to downstream accuracy improvements.
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope severely restricts validity: Evaluation restricted to small, well-studied benchmarks (Imagenette2-320, Caltech101, ImageNet-100). No evaluation on full ImageNet, modern challenging datasets, or tasks beyond image classification. Generalizability to practical scenarios remains undemonstrated.

Weak baseline comparisons and missing related work: Only compares against vanilla KD and one concurrent method (LUGPI from 2024). No comparison to other recent cross-modal distillation or multimodal learning methods. Cannot determine if improvements arise from proposed methods or better engineering.

Theoretical justification is informal and incomplete: Data Processing Inequality argument ignores that decoders optimize reconstruction, not label preservation. The 'capacity interference' concept is vaguely defined and never formally analyzed. Why predictive heads specifically avoid this problem is not rigorously justified. No formal definition of when/why MESSy should outperform L2 matching.

MESSy design choices lack sufficient justification and ablation: (1) Why MSE loss over alternatives (contrastive, focal)? (2) K=3 layers chosen without stated rationale; ablation only in supplementary. (3) How sensitive are results to K? (4) Why average-pool teacher tokens? (5) Why not learn per-layer loss weights? These omissions weaken confidence in the approach.

Emergent synesthesia validation uses arbitrary and insufficiently justified metrics: Cluster counts (50 vs. 150) lack justification. 'Low overlap with class labels' is vague and never quantified. Baseline NMI is already non-negligible in Figure 3; statistical significance of improvements never tested despite only 3 runs. The claim that high NMI proves genuine physical prior learning is not rigorously established.

Generative model quality and robustness completely uncharacterized: No quantitative evaluation of generated 3D or audio latent quality. No ablation on the decision to filter class names from audio captions—this removes potentially useful information but is never justified. Dependency on recent, potentially unstable models (Hunyuan3D-2, Gemma3, Audiocraft all dated 2025) threatens reproducibility but is not acknowledged.

Modest improvements with unclear statistical significance: Gains range from +2.38% (Imagenette2) to +3.40% (Caltech101). With only 3 runs, standard deviations ~0.8%, and no significance testing, confidence in these differences is low. No confidence intervals or statistical hypothesis tests provided.

Incomplete computational cost analysis: While offline generation savings are documented, total training time (including prediction head overhead) and memory costs are not compared. End-to-end cost relative to LUGPI not provided. Only inference cost is confirmed zero (heads discarded).

The synthetic modalities perform poorly in isolation, undermining claimed emergence of true synesthesia: Table 2 shows audio-only accuracy drops to 13.07% on ImageNet-100 and 3D-only to 39.20%. This suggests synthetic modalities encode multimodal artifacts rather than independent physical properties, contradicting the synesthesia emergence narrative.

Reproducibility concerns are substantial: Complex pipeline involving three recent generative models; many hyperparameters only in supplementary. No code release plan stated. Recent model versions (2025) may not remain stable or be widely accessible. Cross-dataset reproduction likely difficult.

Limited failure case analysis and diagnostic depth: No investigation of when the method fails, which classes suffer degradation, or how to predict performance. No cross-dataset evaluation (train synthetic on one dataset, test on another) to assess transfer.

Missing large-scale validation: No evaluation on real paired multimodal datasets (if available) for direct comparison. No evaluation on detection, segmentation, retrieval, or other tasks. Practical utility on modern scales and domains undemonstrated.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated insight about the decode-encode loop inefficiency in generative multimodal training, with clear data processing inequality justification and quantified computational savings (87.7% for 3D, 20.6% for audio)

Comprehensive experimental design with rigorous ablations on modality combinations, evidence that synthetic modalities don't trivially leak labels, and consistent improvements across three datasets (+8.42% on Caltech101, +6.97% on ImageNet-100)
Valuable diagnosis of capacity interference in cross-modal distillation, motivating the predictive MESSy objective as a principled alternative to rigid L2 representation matching

Compelling emergent properties analysis: NMI-based evidence of alignment between student visual features and unobserved modalities, combined with qualitative class-level analysis showing selective modality usage
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (especially Figure 2) and well-structured writing that communicates the motivation and approach effectively
weaknesses: Evaluation limited to small-scale datasets (Imagenette2-320, Caltech101, ImageNet-100), with ImageNet-100 being a tiny subset; no results on full ImageNet or modern large-scale benchmarks, severely limiting generalizability claims

Critical gap in generative model robustness analysis: no ablation on choice or quality of generative models (Hunyuan3D-2, Audiocraft, Gemma3); how results depend on model quality and what happens with weaker generators unexplored; caption filtering methodology underspecified

Insufficient baseline comparisons: only KD and LUGPI tested; missing broader context with other recent multimodal learning methods and alternative distillation approaches; unclear if LUGPI is a strong baseline

Theoretical justification gaps: Data Processing Inequality argument is intuitive but doesn't prove latents always outperform decoded signals; 'capacity interference' concept lacks rigorous grounding; predictive loss superiority over L2 matching not formally analyzed; NMI-performance causality unclear

Methodological clarity issues: information loss from Perceiver resampling (100 tokens per modality) not quantified, aggressive modality dropout (p=0.8) rationale unclear, MESSy depth K=3 unjustified in main paper, substantial result variance (Caltech101: ±0.91)

Reproducibility concerns: hyperparameter choices underjustified, generative model prompt details missing from main text, no code availability mentioned, critical training details (learning rates, schedules) omitted, only 3 runs per experiment

Limited analysis scope: Figure 4 shows only top-improving classes (cherry-picked); no error analysis or failure mode discussion; no sensitivity analysis for design choices (perceiver size, fusion strategy); unclear scalability to larger models or longer training

Generalization questions unaddressed: applicability beyond 3D and audio modalities unclear, scaling properties to large-scale settings unexplored, frozen teacher assumption not justified, training-time computational costs not reported

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: The Decode-Encode Loop inefficiency is a genuine bottleneck in generative data augmentation with clear information-theoretic justification via Data Processing Inequality.

Comprehensive experimental validation with thorough ablations isolating individual contributions, multiple independent runs with standard deviations, and effective label-leakage prevention across multiple datasets.

Novel emergent synesthesia analysis using NMI-based clustering that demonstrates genuine structural alignment with unobserved modalities across both low-level physical and semantic feature spaces (Fig. 6).

Practical efficiency gains quantified concretely: 87.7% reduction in 3D generation time and 23.8% VRAM reduction, with meaningful downstream accuracy improvements (+8.42% on Caltech101, +6.97% on ImageNet-100).
Clear presentation with well-illustrated three-phase pipeline (Fig. 2), accessible mathematical notation, and interpretable class-level analysis of modality-driven improvements (Fig. 7).
Scalability demonstrated on ImageNet-1K showing consistent results (~68% teacher gap recovery), suggesting framework generalizes predictably with dataset size.
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: DLA is a straightforward engineering choice (skip decoding), and MESSy closely resembles existing predictive distillation methods (BYOL, data2vec, AV-data2vec). The restriction to frozen generative models prevents task-specific co-adaptation.

Incomplete theoretical justification: The Data Processing Inequality argument, while intuitive, is loose regarding how decoders inject 'classification-irrelevant noise.' The mechanism by which MESSy avoids capacity interference better than L2 matching lacks rigorous explanation beyond empirical evidence.

Significant persistent teacher-student gaps: 8.87pp on Imagenette, 2.95pp on Caltech101, 3.05pp on ImageNet-100. Student recovers only ~68% of teacher gap on ImageNet-1K, indicating distillation remains a fundamental bottleneck.

Restricted scope and applicability: Evaluation limited to classification only (no detection, segmentation, or other downstream tasks). Dependency on specific off-the-shelf generators limits generalization to domains lacking pre-trained models. Evaluation primarily on standard benchmarks.

Insufficient hyperparameter justification: K=3 layers and β=1.0 for MESSy appear chosen without thorough justification. Aggressive modality dropout (p=0.8) is noted as 'crucial' but lacks sensitivity analysis. Limited comparison with alternative cross-modal distillation approaches beyond LUGPI.

Missing analysis of synthetic data quality effects: No investigation of how generation quality for specific object categories affects distillation performance. Inference cost of multimodal teacher not analyzed. No discussion of negative cases, societal impact, or when the approach fails.

strengths: Identifies genuine inefficiency (decode-encode loop) with concrete computational savings (87.7% time reduction for 3D generation)
Consistent empirical improvements across datasets (DLA +7-11% over raw synthetic data; MESSy +2-3% over LUGPI)
Well-motivated information-theoretic justification via Data Processing Inequality
Comprehensive evaluation within scope: multiple datasets, modality ablations, architectural comparisons
Clear presentation and excellent visualizations, particularly Figure 2
Sensible approach to capacity interference through predictor heads instead of rigid L2 matching
weaknesses: Critical label leakage concern: audio generation uses image-conditioned captioning (Gemma-3); even with class-name filtering, semantic information likely leaks. Audio-Only baseline (13.07%) doesn't rule this out—it only shows noise levels. This undermines core claims about learning physical priors.

Limited technical novelty: DLA is straightforward application of latent representations; MESSy builds directly on BYOL/data2vec/AV-data2vec. Contributions feel incremental rather than methodologically advancing the field.

Overstated 'synesthesia' claims: NMI alignment improvements are modest (0.1-0.15 points, significance unreported). Alignment with unseen modalities could result from better general features or learned correlations, not genuine cross-modal perception. Framing conflates neural network behavior with human synesthesia.
Modest improvements at scale: ImageNet-1K student gains drop to +4.88% versus +10-13% on small datasets, raising scalability concerns. Practical impact for production systems is questionable.

Limited evaluation scope: only classification tested; no detection, segmentation, or retrieval tasks. Synesthesia validation only on same classification datasets. Small benchmarks (Imagenette: 10 classes) dominate main experiments.

Experimental rigor issues: (1) capacity interference evidence (CIFAR-100 linear probe) tested on only one OOD task; (2) hyperparameter choices (p=0.8 dropout, K=3 layers, α/β weights) lack sensitivity analysis; (3) only 3 runs reported; (4) Raw vs Raw+Perc. gap (~1.13pp) suggests architectural confounds in comparison.

Reproducibility challenges: frozen generative models from specific versions; no mentioned code release; complex multi-stage pipeline dependent on evolving external models; key details in supplementary material
Missing critical ablations: no exploration of robustness to different generators, no ablation on caption generation mechanism, no random-caption control experiment for label leakage assessment
Inadequate failure analysis: class-level qualitative analysis (Fig. 7) is anecdotal; no systematic error analysis or discussion of limitations
Incomplete scalability evidence: ImageNet-1K results relegated to one paragraph with no ablations or detailed analysis

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification: The decode-encode loop inefficiency is clearly articulated with rigorous information-theoretic justification (Data Processing Inequality), making the case that undecoded latents should preserve more semantic signal than decoded raw data.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Multiple benchmarks (Imagenette2, Caltech101, ImageNet-100, ImageNet-1K) with 3 independent runs and ± reporting. Thorough ablations isolate DLA and MESSy contributions, including capacity interference evidence via CIFAR-100 linear probe (LUGPI 42.4% vs MESSy 48.1%).

Strong empirical results: DLA teacher achieves +7.39pp over raw synthetic on Caltech101 (+11.37pp over image-only baseline); MESSy student recovers ~68% of teacher gap consistently across datasets; significant computational savings (87.7% faster 3D generation, 23.8% VRAM reduction).

Emergent synesthesia evidence: NMI clustering analysis convincingly shows student's visual space aligns with unseen modalities across both low-level physical features (Hand-Crafted +0.135) and high-level semantics (Deep +0.154), ruling out label co-occurrence explanations.

Careful experimental design: Explicit label leakage prevention in audio caption generation, solo-modality baselines confirm complementary signals (audio-only 13.07%, far above random but below image-only 61.57%), qualitative analysis effectively illustrates class-specific improvements.
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective visualizations (Figures 1-2) that clearly communicate methodological differences across multimodal learning paradigms.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: Predictor-head distillation builds on BYOL, data2vec, and AV-data2vec; MESSy's distinction (targeting auxiliary-modality summaries rather than CLS) is incremental. Using latents instead of raw data is an engineering optimization rather than a fundamental methodological advance. The information-theoretic argument, while elegant, is relatively straightforward.

Dependency on frozen pre-trained generators: Cannot adapt generators to the task, limiting task-specific latent co-adaptation. Generality depends entirely on existing model capabilities; no experiments exploring robustness to generator quality variations or comparing different architectures. Limits practical applicability if task-specific generators become available.

Audio generation bottleneck: Image→caption→audio pipeline introduces potential information loss through intermediate caption step. No analysis of information loss through this bottleneck. Why not explore direct image-to-audio models? Filtering prevents label leakage but could inadvertently filter informative captions.

Limited evaluation scope: Evaluation restricted to image classification only; no detection, segmentation, or other tasks explored. Gains diminish on larger datasets (4.88% ImageNet-1K vs. 13.47% Imagenette2), suggesting saturation with dataset scale and diversity. 'Synesthesia' framing is somewhat metaphorical—learned structure is primarily auxiliary-task prediction.

Underspecified design choices: Modality dropout (p=0.8) during teacher training is aggressive with limited justification beyond 'crucial to prevent over-reliance.' K=3 final layers for MESSy are ablated but sensitivity analysis incomplete. Hyperparameter robustness unclear.

Limited baseline comparisons: LUGPI comparison uses authors' DLA teacher (not original raw-data LUGPI), confounding attribution of improvements. KD baseline is logit-only; missing comparisons with modern KD variants (attention transfer, feature alignment). No comparison with other recent cross-modal distillation methods beyond LUGPI and basic KD.

Diminishing returns at scale: Smaller absolute gains on ImageNet-1K (4.88%) vs. smaller datasets (up to 13.47%) suggest saturation. Teacher-student gap also smaller on ImageNet-1K (7.15% vs. 10-13%), limiting upside and questioning scalability to larger, more diverse datasets.

Incomplete discrete latent analysis: Discrete audio codes from EnCodec quantization artifacts not thoroughly analyzed. No ablation on continuous vs. discrete latent choices. Unclear whether quantization loss is significant relative to claimed decoding artifacts.
